de.reason: Two senses of one English word, split into the `browse-file-picker` and `browse` rulings in `docs/i18n/de/terms.json`. `Durchsuchen…` is the button that opens the system file picker (`servers.sheet.browse`, `settings.adb.browse`), taken from Finder's own `ConnectToWindow.strings` `48.title`. `Durchsehen` is the archives segmented cell (`settings.archives.opt.browse`), which means step INTO the archive and list it like a folder (KDE Dolphin, "Archive durchsehen"). The archive sense cannot take `Durchsuchen`: that is the settled scan/search verb ("Laufwerk wird durchsucht …"), so merging them would tell the reader the app is searching the archive.

Two different checks. `Wird geprüft …` checks a connection or a key (`ai.cloud.checking`, `licensing.dialog.checking`); `Wird gesucht …` is macOS Software Update's own idiom for checking for updates (Nach Updates suchen), so `updates.status.checking` follows Apple. `docs/i18n/de/decisions.md` § Ein englisches Wort, ein deutsches Wort.

`Schließen` closes a dialog, toast, or notice that can come back; `Ausblenden` hides a queue row (`queue.row.dismiss`) or a hint line (`adb.hint.dismiss`) for good. A row can't be closed, and the @key says nothing is undone, retried, or deleted. The `dismiss` ruling in `docs/i18n/de/terms.json`.
`menu.bar.file` is the native File menu, which German macOS calls `Ablage` and its @key asks for Finder's own word; a table column (`suggestedOps.columnFile`) is plain `Datei`.

`Wird gerade indiziert` is the tooltip on ONE image's badge (`fileExplorer.imageIndex.file.indexing`), a passive state; `Indizierung läuft` is the heading over the live progress list (`settings.mediaIndex.progressSummary.title`), a nominal status.
`menu.tag.purple` must be macOS's exact Finder tag color name, which German macOS writes `Lila`; `settings.tint.purple` is Cmdr's own pane-tint palette, where Purple is `Violett`.
`Suchen` is the button that runs the search (`queryUi.bar.runLabel`, an imperative); dialog titles, the tab name, the Settings section, and the task name are the noun `Suche`.

`menu.bar.view` is the native View menu title, which German macOS calls `Darstellung` (a noun that holds the view options); the F3 action is the verb `Ansehen`, kept apart from the show sense `anzeigen`.

`menu.window.zoom` is macOS's Window > Zoom item (the green button), which German macOS calls `Zoomen`; `menu.view.zoom` is the submenu for Cmdr's text size, the noun `Zoom`. The @key asks for macOS's word on the window item.

es.reason: The pronoun agrees in gender with what it covers: `Ambos` for files and folders together (masculine plural), `Ambas` for the two kinds of notification (feminine). Neither fits the other's slot.

`Operación cancelada` titles an error pane and names its subject, like its sibling `Operación interrumpida`; `Cancelado` is a lifecycle status in an operation-log cell. See `docs/i18n/es/decisions.md`.
The menu bar's Edit menu is Apple's own Spanish title `Edición` (Finder); F4 and the context-menu item are the verb `Editar`. Never replace a menu-bar title with the ordinary word.

`Modificación` is Finder's date column (Fecha de modificación) and every date filter; `Modificados` filters the shortcuts the user changed, a masculine plural agreeing with `atajos`, with no date involved.
`Buscar` is the action (dialog title, run button); the Settings sidebar section is a topic, a noun: `Búsqueda`. `Buscar` there would read as a command.
The menu bar's View menu is Apple's own Spanish title `Visualización` (Finder); F3 and the File-menu item are the action `Ver`.

The empty chat invites several questions (`Posez des questions…`); the composer field expects one message (`Posez une question…`). French states a number English leaves open.
The Go menu takes Finder's exact word, `Précédent` (macOS fr has no bare `Retour`); the network and wizard buttons are Cmdr surfaces and say `Retour`. See `docs/i18n/fr/terms.json` `back`.
`Opération annulée` titles a panel and names the implied subject, like `Opération interrompue`; `Annulé` is an operation-log status pill.
`Édition` is Finder's Edit MENU title; `Modifier` is the verb on the F4 button and the context menu.
`Modifié` is the date column and filter; `Modifiés` is the shortcuts filter, agreeing with the plural shortcuts you changed.
The progress dialog title keeps its ellipsis (the dots say progress); the operation-log status cell has none, so it spells out `en cours`, parallel to `En cours` for running.
`En cours d'exécution` is a server PROCESS that is up; `En cours` is a task or operation in progress.
`Rechercher` is the action (dialog title, run button); the Settings sidebar section is a topic, a noun: `Recherche`.

The title and the command name the action in general (`Envoyer un retour`); the send button acts on the message in front of you (`Envoyer le retour`), like `Envoyer un rapport d'incident` / `Envoyer le rapport`.
The menu bar's View menu is Finder's `Présentation`; F3 and the File-menu item are the action `Visualiser`.
The window's green-button action is Finder's `Réduire/agrandir` (Window > Zoom); the text-size submenu keeps `Zoom`.

hu.reason: `Bájtok` is the progress bar's row label, paired with `Fájlok`; `Bájt` is the size-unit picker's button, next to `kB`, `MB`, `GB`.

`Forrás` is the transfer dialog's heading, paired with `Cél` (Total Commander and Double Commander hu); `Innen` is the inline label before a scan-phase source path.
`Bíbor` is one of Finder's seven tag colors, verbatim (`TG_COLOR_3`); `Lila` is Cmdr's own 12-color pane tint, where the everyday color name is right.

`Visszagörgetés…` is the progress window's title, the ellipsis carrying the ongoing state; the operation log's status cell is `Visszagörgetés folyamatban`, beside capability cells (`Visszagörgethető`), where the bare noun would be ambiguous.
`Kijelölés` is the file-selection menu and action; `Válassz` is the dropdown placeholder, where the user picks an option rather than selecting files.

`Aanmaakdatum` is Finder's column header (Date Created); the date balloon lists participles (`Aangemaakt`, `Laatst gewijzigd`, `Laatst geopend`), so it takes the participle.
`Gereed` is an operation's lifecycle status (macOS AppKit Done → Gereed). `Klaar` is the word a screen reader appends to a finished checklist step, where a plain adjective reads right.

The menu bar's Edit menu is Apple's own title `Wijzig`; F4 and the context-menu item open a file in an editor, which this catalog names `Bewerk`. Never replace a menu-bar title with the ordinary word.
The menu bar's File menu is Apple's own Dutch title `Archief`; the suggested-ops column names an ordinary file, `Bestand`.
`Van` / `Naar` are a paired heading set in the transfer dialog (Total Commander and Double Commander nl). `Vanuit:` is the inline label in front of a source path during the scan phase.
`Bewerkingsdatum` is Finder's Date Modified column and the date filters. The keyboard-shortcuts filter means shortcuts the user changed, with no date involved, so it takes `Gewijzigd`.
`Bezig` is an operation or task in progress (the queue's state word). `Actief` is a local AI server process that is up, which Dutch doesn't call `bezig`.
`Zoek` is the button that starts a search (bare-stem imperative, macOS Search → Zoek). `Zoeken` names the feature: the window title, the Settings section, the onboarding feature row.

`Selecteer` is the menu-bar menu for file selection (imperative). `Selecteren` is the onboarding feature-row name, parallel to `Zoeken`. `Kies` is the dropdown placeholder, where the user picks an option rather than selecting files.
Buttons and menu items take the bare-stem imperative `Verstuur foutrapport`; the dialog title takes the infinitive `Foutrapport versturen`, the house form for window titles.
Buttons and menu items take the imperative `Verstuur feedback`; the dialog title takes the infinitive `Feedback versturen`.
The button takes the imperative `Verstuur rapport`; the crash dialog's title takes the infinitive `Rapport versturen`.
The View-menu item is the imperative `Toon verborgen bestanden`; the Settings checkbox label is infinitive-last, `Verborgen bestanden tonen`, the house form of every settings label.

Three different actions: `Herstel` is Apple's Edit > Undo (text undo, must match macOS); `Zet terug` is Finder's Put Back, which the trash toast literally performs; `Ongedaan maken` reverts an Ask Cmdr rename run.
The menu bar's View menu is Apple's own title `Weergave`; F3 and the File-menu item show a file, which is `Toon`.
`Zoom` is Cmdr's text zoom submenu; the Window menu's Zoom item (fill the screen) is Apple's own Dutch title `Vergroot/verklein`.

pt.reason: Gender agreement, not drift: `Ambos` agrees with files and folders (`queryUi.filters.type.both`), `Ambas` with notifications (`…downloadsNotifications.opt.both`).

Two senses of one English word, each ruled separately in `docs/i18n/pt/terms.json` (`browse-file-picker`, `browse`). `Escolher…` is the button that opens the system file picker (`servers.sheet.browse`, `settings.adb.browse`), taken from Apple's own `Choose…` → `Escolher…`. `Navegar` is the archives segmented cell (`settings.archives.opt.browse`), which means step inside and list like a folder (macOS Finder VoiceOver, Total Commander pt-BR). Apple never says `Navegar` for picking a file, and the archive sense is never `Escolher`, so one word for both would be wrong on whichever surface lost.
Number agreement, not drift: `Modificado` is a file's date column and filter, `Modificados` is the keyboard-shortcuts filter for the shortcuts the user changed (`shortcuts.section.filterModified`).

Noun vs verb, both Finder's: `Pré-visualização` labels a preview panel or sample (`askCmdr.renameReview.preview`, `settings.appearance.datePreviewLabel`), `Pré-visualizar` is the command (`commands.fileQuickLook.other.label`).
Gender agreement, not drift: `Revertida` agrees with the operation (`operationLog.rollback.rolledBack`), `Revertido` with the item (`operationLog.outcome.rolledBack`).
Two senses: `Em andamento` is a task in progress (`operationLog.status.running`, matching `queue.row.status`), `Em execução` is a local AI server that is up (`ai.local.statusRunning`).
Noun vs verb: `Busca` names the Settings section beside nouns like `Aparência` and `Indexação` (`settings.section.search`); `Buscar` is the button that runs a search and the dialog title.

sv.reason: `Kontrollerar` verifies something you already have (an API key, a license); `Söker` looks for something that may exist (`updates.status.checking`), matching the update family's `Sök efter uppdateringar`. See `docs/i18n/sv/terms.json` `check`.
The menu bar's File menu is Apple's own Swedish title `Arkiv` (Finder, AppKit); the suggested-ops column names an ordinary file, `Fil`.
`Ändrad` describes one file's date (the column and the date filters); the keyboard-shortcuts filter chip `Ändrade` filters a set of commands, so the participle agrees in the plural.
`Körs` is a local AI server process that is up; `Pågår` is a file operation in progress, the queue and log status. macOS Finder has the same pair (medan Finder körs / en annan åtgärd pågår).
`Markera` marks files (the menu-bar Select menu, macOS Markera allt); `Välj` picks an option, which is what a dropdown placeholder asks for.
The menu bar's View menu is Apple's own Swedish title `Innehåll` (Finder and Safari); F3 and the context-menu item open the viewer, `Visa`.
Finder splits them: the text-zoom submenu is the noun `Zoom`, Window > Zoom is the verb `Zooma`.

vi.reason: macOS vi draws this line: going back in the folder HISTORY is `Trở lại` (Finder Go > Back, `menu.go.back`), returning to the previous SCREEN or step inside a flow is `Quay lại` (Setup Assistant, the Apple ID sheets; the network browser and the onboarding wizard). See `docs/i18n/vi/terms.json` `back`.

`Đã sửa đổi` is the date column (Finder Get Info "Modified:"); `shortcuts.section.filterModified` filters commands whose shortcut the user CHANGED, so `Đã thay đổi`. One word would make the shortcut filter read like a date filter. See `docs/i18n/vi/terms.json` `modified`.

zh.reason: Two senses. Beside `macOS` as a colour SOURCE (the date and size colour options) the Latin `App` stays, as Apple zh-CN writes it; as a shortcut SCOPE (`shortcuts.scope.app`) it's the translated scope word `应用`, matching its all-Chinese sibling scopes. See `docs/i18n/zh/terms.json` `app`.
`返回` is navigation back to the previous place (macOS zh-CN renders Back, Go Back, and go back all as `返回`); `上一步` is the onboarding wizard's previous step, paired with `下一步`.
`两者` is a bare toggle cell beside `文件` / `文件夹`; `两者都用` is a radio option that must pair with its sibling `都不用`, so it needs the verb.

`完成` is the word a screen reader announces after a checklist step (macOS System Settings Done → `完成`); `已完成` is an operation's lifecycle status value, a perfective state like its siblings `已取消` / `已跳过`.
`修改日期` is Finder's Date Modified column and the date filters; the keyboard-shortcuts filter means shortcuts the user changed, with no date involved, so it's `已修改`.
Tight mode chips use the short `正则`; the viewer's regex toggle shows only a `.*` glyph, so its tooltip and accessible name spell out `正则表达式` for screen-reader users.
`运行中` is a local AI server process that is up; `进行中` is a task or operation in progress, the queue and log status value.
`正在扫描` is the in-progress tooltip with an ellipsis; `扫描` is a step NAME in the two-step progress indicator, the same split AppKit makes (Searching → `搜索`, Searching… → `正在搜索…`).
`选择` is the verb and the menu-bar title; `请选择` is the dropdown placeholder (English `Select...`), a prompt that nothing is chosen yet.
`无法连接` is a host the network browser can't connect to; `无法访问` is a tab whose folder or volume can't be reached, where there may be no connection at all (an ejected drive).
The menu bar's View menu is Apple's own zh-CN title `显示`; F3 and the context-menu item open the file in the viewer, which is `查看`.

zh-Hant.reason: Two senses of one English word. The Settings colour options mean the app AS A SOURCE of a colour (kept as the Latin `App`, per the brand-word rule); the shortcuts scope means `in-app`, which needs `App 內` to contrast with the system-wide scope beside it.

`返回` is navigation back (history, network browser, the Go menu). The onboarding wizard's `上一步` is the previous STEP of a sequence, which Traditional Chinese names differently; `返回` there would suggest leaving the wizard.

`兩者` answers `which of these two?` in the search type filter. The notification setting asks WHERE to notify and picks both channels, so it reads as `兩者都用` (use both), which is a verb phrase, not an enumeration.

`完成` is the visually-hidden word a screen reader appends to a finished checklist step (`Find files. Done.`), where a bare adjective is right. `已完成` is an operation's lifecycle status in the log, where the perfective aspect marks a finished run.

`修改日期` is the Finder column header and the date filters, where `Modified` abbreviates `Date modified`. The keyboard-shortcuts filter chip means `commands whose shortcut YOU changed`, with no date involved, so it takes `已修改`.

Total Commander, the source the glossary already cites for the full `正規表示式`, ships its own short chip `正規式` (WCMD.LNG IDs 5615/6626). The search-mode chips are tight and take it; `viewer.search.regex` is an aria label plus tooltip whose visible text is the fixed `.*` glyph, so it has room for the full form and a screen reader wants it. Bare `正規` is banned in both: it's a bound morpheme, and Microsoft's only `正規*` entries are `正規化` = normalization.
`執行中` is a local AI server PROCESS that is up. `進行中` is an operation in progress in the log. Traditional Chinese splits these; a running process is not a task making progress.

The spinner tooltip renders `Scanning…` and takes the progressive `正在掃描…`. The progress dialog's step chip is a two-word stage NAME in a fixed-width indicator, so it takes the bare `掃描`, matching the other stage chips beside it.

`選取` is the menu-bar Select menu and the verb. `ui.select.placeholder` is the empty state of a dropdown, which Traditional Chinese phrases as an invitation (`請選擇`, please choose) rather than a bare verb.

The crash dialog's TITLE asks the question (`要傳送報告嗎`), which is the house pattern for a confirming dialog title in this catalog; the button below it is the bare action `傳送報告`. English reuses one string for both surfaces.

The canonical split. `檢視` is the verb: open the file viewer (F3), which is `commands.fileView` and `menu.file.view`. `menu.bar.view` is the View MENU, which macOS Traditional calls `顯示方式` (display mode) because it holds the view-mode choices. Merging them would rename either the F3 command or the menu.

The status-bar selection summary drops the measure word (`{目錄}`) because it composes as `3 / 10 目錄` with a `/` connector already separating the numbers; the scan stats render a bare tally (`4 個目錄`) and need it. Same word, two grammatical frames.
Same frame split as the `dirs` noun above: `{檔案}` in the `/`-connected status-bar summary, `{個檔案}` after a bare tally in the delete and transfer scan stats.
